Hi there! When it comes to checking figures, I’d rate myself a solid 10 out of 10. In accounts work, even a misplaced decimal or missed entry can ripple through ledgers, tax filings, and client trust, so I’ve built a few reliable, repeatable habits to keep everything accurate. I always cross-reference entries against original invoices and bank statements, use spreadsheet formulas and conditional formatting to flag anomalies, and run a quick three-way match before locking any report. Taking that extra minute to verify not only keeps the books balanced but also gives everyone peace of mind. I’m always happy to share my checklists or walk through my verification steps if it helps!

Rating: 10

When verifying figures, I operate at the highest level of scrutiny. Every number is treated as a claim that must be substantiated, not merely accepted. My process begins with source-document reconciliation, followed by independent recalculation of all formulas, subtotals, and cross-references. I systematically trace entries through the full audit trail, verify rounding and currency conventions, and apply analytical procedures to detect anomalies or deviations from expected patterns. In financial reporting, a single misplaced decimal or overlooked adjustment can cascade into material misstatements, so I employ a multi-pass verification protocol: initial reconciliation, blind recalculation, peer-style cross-checking, and final logical consistency review. This disciplined, methodical approach is not optional—it is the foundation of reliable financial assurance. Given this uncompromising standard, my carefulness is absolute.

I’d rate myself a solid 10. In accounting, accuracy isn’t just a nice-to-have—it’s the foundation of everything we do. A misplaced decimal, a duplicated entry, or a missed reconciliation can quickly snowball into reporting errors, cash flow surprises, or compliance headaches. That’s why I’ve built a few dependable habits into my workflow: I always cross-check figures against source documents, use built-in spreadsheet validations to catch mismatches early, run a quick logical review on high-value or unusual entries, and keep a tidy, step-by-step checklist for month-end and quarterly closes. If something doesn’t balance on the first pass, I don’t just move on—I trace it back, double-check the supporting paperwork, and resolve it before it impacts the wider team. Being careful with numbers is how I keep processes running smoothly and give stakeholders the confidence that the books are truly in order. Happy to share my reconciliation templates or checking routines if you ever need them!
